THE OBSERVATORY

Two light trains follow the chaotic orbit, sweeping through its lobes and leaving soft trails. The original point cloud stays beneath them.

Compare scaled opacity with fixed per-point opacity. Scaling can darken faint points; fixed opacity adds more light as density rises. Lines connect the selected samples in time order, without closing the orbit. More samples and planes take more GPU work.

All planes share the z axis. Steps add angular bisectors, not equal physical distances. Every sheet is a fresh orthogonal projection of the same 3D samples.

A precomputed angular average of the same orbit, smoothed onto a 160³ density grid. Every sample sweeps a circle as the projection plane turns. 512 angular samples approximate the continuous limit. This is a density visualization, not a new solid attractor. The field is static; the camera orbits it.

Vertical orbit makes a full overhead-to-underside circuit. The camera stays aimed at the center and rotates continuously through the poles.

The underlying system

180,000 fixed-step Chen–Čelikovský samples preserve the original 3D shape. Two smooth light trains advance along a real 12,000-sample segment. The ends fade instead of joining unrelated points. Camera and illumination loop exactly; the chaotic solution itself is not periodic.
